_comment: Product source files permitted to exceed the 1000-line limit. POLICY-OWNED: the contents are set by
the reviewer, not inferred from whatever happens to be oversized today. Adding a path here is a
decision; removing one is just bookkeeping after a file is cleared.
Approved by comms-senior-dev on 2026-08-13, verbatim: 'Allowlist should be explicit and policy-owned,
not inferred from whatever is currently oversized. The currently justified product allowlist is the
ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH, read by both gates -- service/tests/test_no_new_oversized_source_file.py and
mcp/stdio/tests/no-new-oversized-source-file.test.js. Two copies of a list like this is the forked-
constant class the whole v0.5.x series has been removing; a duplicated allowlist would drift silently
and each gate would then enforce a different policy.
PATHS, NOT BASENAMES. The first version of these gates matched on basename, which would have exempted
any file called app.js or server.js anywhere in the tree. Repo-relative, forward slashes.
Both gates fail if a listed path no longer exists or has dropped below the limit, so this list shrinks
honestly and cannot rot into names nobody re-checked.

allowed.reason: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-14 at 2,520 lines (was 6,331 at the start of v0.5.4). The previous reason quoted '7 of 47 top-level functions, 88 lines movable, the file reaches ~2,918' and is WITHDRAWN as an underestimate — far more than 88 lines have since moved, by measuring GROUPS rather than functions and by running an in-degree survey (scratchpad hubs.mjs, built on the reconstruction proof's own declarationSpan) to find the shared names holding the file together. That survey is what surfaced the claim-failure trackers. What remains is genuinely blocked, and every remaining closure is >=36 lines and falls into exactly one of four categories: the scheduler loops, which docs/JS_SERVER_REMAINDER_PACKET.md option C calls 'a redesign, not a relocation' that 'touches the code path that took the managed fleet down'; the SWEEPS (runManagedTeardownForBridge, runBootSurvivorSweep) awaiting operator go-ahead; spawnTriggeredAgent, which has its own packet; and the shutdown chain, which reaches the sweeps. The A-vs-B question in JS_SERVER_JS_PROOF_PACKET.md is already RESOLVED (B shipped; activeServerUrl() exists) — do not re-escalate it.

RE-MEASURED AND SIMULATED 2026-08-14 at 3,612 lines (was 5,081). Zero closed groups remain: six hubs each pull ~75 declarations because they all reach `refresh` — one mutually-recursive render orchestrator. BUT 'break that component' does NOT clear this file, and an earlier version of this reason implied it would. Simulated on a scratch copy: extracting all 74 component declarations leaves 2,109 lines (2.1x the limit) with ZERO dead-import relief, because the 720-line top-level init/handler block that stays still uses every import and cannot travel with the component (it is statements, not declarations, so there is no span to relocate). A three-phase path DOES reach the limit and is costed in docs/APP_JS_STATE_MODULE_PACKET.md: component -> 2,109, then the 23 action handlers it was blocking -> 1,699, then the top-level block as init()/installHandlers() -> ~984. Phase 2 is ordinary relocation but does not exist until phase 1 lands; phase 1 must split into several modules since 1,578 lines cannot be one; phase 3 needs a reconstruction-proof shape for top-level statements that does not exist yet. The ~16-line final margin is thin and is not a pass. Listed until an operator scopes that work — it is measured, not unreachable.
